Regarding "mā" (what/He who) there are two opinions, which we have mentioned at His saying: ﴿And by He who built it﴾ [ash-Shams: 5]. Regarding ﴿the male and the female﴾ there are two opinions.

The first: they are Adam and Eve. This was said by Ibn al-Sa'ib and Muqatil.

(p-146) The second: it is general, mentioned by al-Mawardi.

Regarding the occasion of revelation of this surah there are two opinions.

The first: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, bought Bilal from Umayyah and Ubayy, the two sons of Khalaf, for a striped garment and ten uqiyah, and freed him. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿By the night﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾, meaning the effort of Abu Bakr, and of Umayyah and Ubayy. This was said by ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud.

When the man climbed the palm tree to take its dates, dates would sometimes fall, and the poor man's children would take them. The man would come down from his palm tree to take the date from their hands, and if he found it in the mouth of one of them (p-147) he would insert his finger until he brought it out. The third: he gave what was Allah's right upon him, said by Qatadah.

The second: he feared miserliness, said by Mujahid.

The third: he feared the prohibitions of Allah which He forbade, said by Qatadah.

The fourth: the blessings of Allah upon him, said by ʿAtaʾ.

One: when he falls into Hell, said by Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah. The meaning: when he plunges into it.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 92, verses 12–21:

Allah's words: ﴿Indeed, it is upon Us to guide﴾. Al-Zajjaj (the grammarian Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj) said: The meaning is: Indeed, it is upon Us to make clear the path of guidance from the path of misguidance. ﴿And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life﴾, meaning: so let them be sought from Us. ﴿So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes﴾, meaning: it is kindled and flares. ﴿None will enter it except the most wretched﴾, meaning: the polytheist ﴿who denied﴾ the Messenger ﴿and turned away﴾ from faith. Abu Ubayda said: ﴿al-ashqa (the most wretched)﴾ carries the sense of ﴿al-shaqiyy (the wretched)﴾. The Arabs place the form ﻓَعْلَى (af'al) in the position of the active participle (fa'il). Tarafa said:

Men wished that I would die, and if I die, that is a path in which I am not unique.

Al-Zajjaj said: This is the verse on account of which the people of irja' (the Murji'ah, who deferred judgement on the sinner) claimed that none enters the Fire except a disbeliever. But the matter is not as they supposed. This is a Fire described specifically, and the people of the Fire have degrees. Had it been that everyone who does not associate partners [with Allah] is not punished, then His words ﴿and He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills﴾ [al-Nisa': 48] would have no benefit, and "and He forgives what is less than that" would be a statement with no meaning.

Allah's words: ﴿And the most righteous will be kept away from it﴾, meaning: it will be kept far from him, and he will be placed aside from it, ﴿the most righteous﴾, meaning: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), according to the consensus of the exegetes ﴿who gives his wealth to purify himself﴾, meaning: he seeks to be pure in the sight of Allah, and does not seek showing off, nor reputation. ﴿And for no one has he any favour [that must be] repaid﴾, meaning: he did not do that as recompense for a favour bestowed upon him.

Ata related from Ibn Abbas that when Abu Bakr bought Bilal after he had been being tortured, the polytheists said: Abu Bakr did not do that except because of a favour Bilal had done for him. So Allah revealed: ﴿And for no one has he any favour [that must be] repaid﴾ ﴿except seeking the countenance of his Lord, the Most High﴾, meaning: except seeking the reward of his Lord. Al-Farra' said: "illa" here means "lakin (but rather)", and "ibtigha'" is in the accusative by an implied verb of spending. The meaning is: he spends only seeking the countenance of his Lord.

Allah's words: ﴿And he will surely be pleased﴾, meaning: with what is given to him of reward in Paradise.
